stories.why_it_matters: A short-range strike missile close to entering service adds to India's own defence capability and to orders for local defence makers.
stories.note: Single source: All India Radio (citing Defence Ministry).

image.alt: A Pralay missile lifts off from a mobile launcher truck in a cloud of smoke

impact.why: A missile nearing induction points to future orders for defence suppliers.

stories.headline: DRDO test-fires Pralay missile in user trials; induction now close, ministry says
stories.summary: DRDO flight-tested its home-built quasi-ballistic missile Pralay from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island off Odisha on Thursday. The Defence Ministry says all test goals were met as part of user evaluation trials with the armed forces present, and that the system's induction is now imminent.

stories.note: Single source: All India Radio (minister's remarks).

impact.why: Steady clean-energy investment supports power and renewable equipment firms.

stories.headline: Renewable investment to top $220 billion goal by 2030, says Pralhad Joshi
stories.summary: Energy minister Pralhad Joshi says India will beat its $220 billion investment target for adding 190 GW of clean power by 2030, after ₹7 lakh crore flowed into the sector in two years. He says non-fossil capacity now stands at 310 GW and the 500 GW target for 2030 will be met on time.

stories.note: Single source: All India Radio (minister's remarks).

impact.why: A common trading platform could change how coal and ore are priced and sold.

stories.headline: Coal and mineral exchanges to launch soon, says minister Kishan Reddy
stories.summary: Coal and Mines Minister G. Kishan Reddy says the Centre will soon launch exchanges for coal and minerals such as iron ore, bauxite, limestone and critical minerals, with about 90% of the groundwork done. He says states' income from non-coal mining has risen from about ₹13,000 crore in 2014-15 to over ₹70,000 crore.

stories.headline: Centre tells Supreme Court it will set up panel to review UGC equity rules
stories.summary: The government told the Supreme Court it is forming a special committee to review the UGC's 2026 rules against caste discrimination on campuses, which the court had stayed. The bench under Chief Justice Surya Kant said all students' interests must be protected and adjourned the case for four weeks.

stories.why_it_matters: Any real progress towards ending the war could ease energy prices and sanctions risk worldwide.
stories.note: Meeting confirmed by both sources; the 'very close' view is Trump's own claim.

image.alt: Donald Trump gestures while speaking in the Oval Office

impact.why: Hopes of a Russia-Ukraine deal can ease supply worries for energy.

stories.headline: Trump says Russia-Ukraine deal 'very close' after meeting Putin envoy Dmitriev
stories.summary: Trump met Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev at the White House on Thursday and says a peace deal is near, one that could involve all of Europe; he gave no details. Dmitriev was in Washington for a meeting of Russian and Ukrainian officials hosted by Melania Trump to build on a short Kherson truce.

stories.why_it_matters: Fresh US threats keep oil near $100, which hurts India's import bill and the rupee.
stories.note: Single source: Al Jazeera. Statements by Trump and Iran; no new attack confirmed.

impact.why: Threats of new US strikes raise the risk to Gulf oil supply.
War fears add to safe-haven demand.

stories.headline: Trump says US may have to 'destroy' the rest of Iran
stories.summary: Trump says the US may have to destroy what is left of Iran and that rebuilding would take 25 years, adding on social media that people will 'know soon enough'. He did not say what action he meant. Iran said on Thursday that states helping any US attack would be legitimate targets.

stories.why_it_matters: A mutual-defence pact that includes Pakistan matters for India's security planning.
stories.headline: Turkiye's parliament ratifies defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan
stories.summary: Turkish lawmakers approved the Mecca defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan by 279 votes to 119 on Thursday. The 10-year pact says members must immediately help any member that is attacked, similar to NATO's Article 5.

stories.headline: Bomb threats hit more than a dozen passenger flights across Europe
stories.summary: More than a dozen flights in Europe got bomb threats on Thursday, forcing diversions and checks in France, Bulgaria, Poland, Romania, Belgium and the Czech Republic. An Aer Lingus jet was diverted to a French air base; no dangerous objects were reported found. EU air safety agency EASA says it is monitoring.

stories.headline: Paraguay's President Peña resigns after collapse of digital bank ueno
stories.summary: Santiago Peña quit on Thursday as calls for his removal grew over the failure of lender ueno, which left about 3 million customers locked out of their accounts. The central bank stepped in after finding ueno broke solvency rules; Vice President Pedro Alliana is set to take over.

stories.why_it_matters: A strong jobs number would raise Fed hike bets and could pressure the rupee and foreign flows into India.
stories.note: Dollar index level from Yahoo Finance data; jobs forecast and FedWatch odds from CNBC.

impact.why: The jobs report will steer Fed hike bets and the dollar's next move.
A risk-off mood and Fed hike odds can weigh on the rupee.

stories.headline: Dollar steady near 101.6 before US jobs data; markets see 70% chance of Fed hike
stories.summary: The dollar index held near 101.6 in Asian trade as investors waited for Friday's US October jobs report, where about 59,000 new jobs and 4.2% unemployment are expected, CNBC said. CME FedWatch shows about a 70% chance of a quarter-point Fed rate rise on 9 December. The rupee last closed at 94.47 per dollar.

stories.note: Single source each: Bank of Canada (Macklem); CTV News (budget figure).

impact.why: Signals of further hikes support the Canadian dollar.

stories.headline: Bank of Canada's Macklem says more hikes may be needed; budget deficit at C$62.3bn
stories.summary: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem told senators the bank may need to raise rates further after last week's hike to 2.5%, but will move carefully, one meeting at a time. Hours later, Ottawa's budget put this year's deficit at C$62.3 billion, slightly below the spring estimate.

stories.why_it_matters: A global tech rout usually hits Indian IT stocks and foreign flows, so Indian markets may struggle to extend their six-day rally today.

image.alt: A trader watches screens full of red market charts on a trading floor

impact.why: Fears of curbs on data centres are hitting AI and chip valuations.
A global tech sell-off tends to drag Indian IT shares and foreign flows.
Bitcoin fell about 5% as risk appetite collapsed.

stories.headline: Wall Street's worst day since April 2025: Nasdaq sinks 5.5% on AI sell-off
stories.summary: The Nasdaq fell 5.5% to 24,315 and into correction, the S&P 500 lost 4.4% to 7,354 and the Dow dropped 1,833 points, or 3.4%. Chip and AI stocks led: Micron and AMD fell about 17%, Broadcom about 10% and Nvidia about 9%, on fears a Democratic Congress will slow data centre building. The VIX fear gauge touched 28.

stories.why_it_matters: The rout reaching Asia raises the risk of heavy foreign selling across emerging markets, including India.

impact.why: A deep Asian sell-off points to a weak open for Indian shares.

stories.headline: Asia follows: Kospi plunges over 8% with trading halt, Nikkei enters bear market
stories.summary: South Korea's Kospi fell more than 8% below 5,000 on Friday, triggering a 20-minute trading halt, and Japan's Nikkei slid about 6% into a bear market, CNBC reported. Chip makers led the fall: SoftBank lost 11.6%, TSMC 9.6%, SK Hynix over 8% and Samsung 7%.
